name: Question Pair
job: Set what the reader said beside the question worth asking about it, one row a point, so every question visibly comes from their own words.

anatomy.role: Surface card, hairline border, rows split by hairlines; two equal columns split by a hairline
Mono, uppercase, label step, on a tinted bar; the answer column head in cyan
Their point, in their words, secondary text

states.name: Two rows
states.note: The usual shape: two to five rows.

states.name: Phone width
states.note: Below 640px the columns stack; the answer column head hides and each ask gets an inline cyan lead.

use_when: Every question or recommendation traces to something the counterpart said, and showing that trace is the point.
A proposal or brief where the reader should recognise their own words before they read yours.
avoid_when: Do not paraphrase the left column into your vocabulary; it is their words or it is not this part.
Do not use it for a two-column comparison of options; that is a table, not a question pair.

data.note: Column heads, for example `What you raised` and `Worth asking`.
One row a point. Plain text.

access: Column heads are `h3` elements; each row reads said, then ask, in source order.
On a phone the ask carries a visible text lead, so the pairing never depends on colour or column position.
The grid uses `minmax(0, 1fr)`, so large text wraps inside the cell.

used_by.name: Louisville proposal (louisville.arcs.care/proposal), page-local today; swap in after the send

gates: `kit_specimen.py --check` (in scripts): this page matches its spec.
`kit_primitive_sync.py --check`: every page that marks this block carries it line for line.
`artifact_wrap_lint.py` and `page_gate.py` on every page that carries it; sweep 360 to 1440, including 700 to 1000.
